name: Can I replace my kitchen sink without changing the countertops?

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my kitchen sink without changing the countertops?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can keep your old countertop if the new sink fits the existing opening or has a slightly larger footprint. If the new sink is smaller, it will leave gaps that cannot be bridged. Expanding a cutout in laminate, butcher block, or composite materials is relatively straightforward, but enlarging cutouts in granite, marble, or quartz requires specialized cutting equipment on-site. When keeping existing counters, measuring your cutout radius and depth is critical before selecting a replacement sink.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, provided the new sink matches the current cutout or is slightly larger. A smaller sink will leave unfillable gaps in the counter.
